interest: Japanese naval goodwill in Mexico and tanker before oil expropriation.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.3312, covering March 1933 to March 1938) documents visits and prospective calls of Japanese naval training vessels, government ships, and commercial tankers to Mexican Pacific and Gulf ports, along with close diplomatic and intelligence surveillance by the United States Embassy in Mexico City and regional U.S. consulates. Major events recorded include the April–May 1933 goodwill cruise of the Imperial Japanese Navy training squadron (cruisers Yakumo and Iwate and the fuel transport Taibun Maru) under Vice Admiral Gengo Hyakutake to Acapulco and Manzanillo, featuring an official overland delegation to Mexico City, meetings with President Abelardo L. Rodríguez and Mexican cabinet secretaries, and an armed robbery of a Japanese Legation vehicle at Tierra Colorada; the June 1935 port call of the training ship Nippon Maru (Ministry of Education) at Ensenada, Baja California, en route to the San Diego Exposition; the September 1936 training cruise of the Yakumo and Iwate under Vice Admiral Zengo Yoshida to Manzanillo and Mexico City, marked by elaborate military toasts, a fatal launch accident at Manzanillo, and Japanese cadets repairing washed-out railway lines near Atenquique; and strictly confidential March 1938 intelligence reporting the expected arrival at Tampico and Tuxpan of the Japanese tanker Itsukushima Maru to lift Poza Rica crude oil from Petromex under charter by British intermediary Centralamer, Ltd., on the immediate eve of the Mexican oil expropriation.

subfiles.about: Reports that the Mexican Government granted permission for Japanese naval training ships Yakumo and Iwate to visit Mexican ports in April and May 1933.
subfiles.summary: Lane reports Mexican permission for the Yakumo and Iwate to visit Acapulco and Manzanillo, 1933.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2338 from Arthur Bliss Lane on Visit of Japanese Training Ships

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet and attached extract from Acapulco consular report No. 33 noting the arrival of Japanese naval vessels and local conditions.
subfiles.summary: File note and extract: two Japanese cruisers and a supply ship at Acapulco, April 30–May 6, 1933.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet and Extract regarding Acapulco Report No. 33 on Japanese Naval Vessels

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum noting that Despatch No. 49 from Mexico reports on the Japanese gunboat visit in detail and need not be read.
subfiles.summary: FE memo saying despatch No. 49 on the Yakumo and Iwate need not be read.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs on Despatch No. 49

subfiles.about: Comprehensive report on the courtesy visit of Japanese training ships Yakumo and Iwate to Acapulco and their reception in Mexico City.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Josephus Daniels details the courtesy visit of Japanese training ships Yakumo and Iwate and the fuel transport Taibun Maru to Acapulco beginning April 30, 1933. Vice Admiral Gengo Hyakutake and thirty-six officers and cadets traveled to Mexico City, holding courtesy meetings with President Abelardo L. Rodríguez, Secretary of War Lázaro Cárdenas, and other cabinet ministers, followed by a formal reception hosted by Japanese Minister Hori. The despatch quotes Admiral Hyakutake's public tribute to Mexican history and the Boy Heroes, describes the armed highway robbery of a Japanese Legation automobile near Tierra Colorada and the recovery of stolen funds, and outlines the squadron's itinerary toward the Panama Canal Zone and Honolulu.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 49 from Josephus Daniels on the Visit of Japanese Gunboats Yakumo and Iwate

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Ambassador Josephus Daniels' Despatch No. 49 detailing the courtesy visit of Japanese training ships to Mexico.
subfiles.summary: This is a duplicate record copy of Ambassador Josephus Daniels' Despatch No. 49 of May 11, 1933. It recounts the arrival of the Japanese training fleet at Acapulco, the automotive journey of Vice Admiral Hyakutake and his staff to Mexico City, their meetings with President Rodríguez and cabinet officials, and the diplomatic reception at the Japanese Legation. It also includes the full account of the robbery of the Legation vehicle at Tierra Colorada and the scheduled departure for the Canal Zone and Honolulu.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Copy of Despatch No. 49 on the Visit of Japanese Gunboats Yakumo and Iwate

subfiles.about: Reports the arrival of Japanese training ships at Manzanillo and press allegations of discourtesies by customs officials at Acapulco.
subfiles.summary: Daniels reports the training ships at Manzanillo and a press claim of customs discourtesy at Acapulco.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 151 from Josephus Daniels on Japanese Training Ships at Manzanillo

subfiles.about: Notes that the Japanese training vessel Nippon Maru is recorded in Lloyd's Register as owned by the Japanese Department of Education.
subfiles.summary: FE memo: the Nippon Maru belongs to Japan's Department of Education.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs on Ownership of Nippon Maru

subfiles.about: Reports on the visit of the Japanese training ship Nippon Maru to Ensenada and courtesies extended by the American consulate.
subfiles.summary: Smale reports the Nippon Maru's 1935 visit to Ensenada and his courtesies to its officers.
subfiles.title: Despatch from William A. Smale on Visit of Japanese Training Ship Nippon Maru to Ensenada

subfiles.about: Transmits an account prepared by the Embassy's Military Attaché regarding the visit of Japanese training ships Iwate and Yakumo.
subfiles.summary: Daniels sends the Military Attaché's report on the Iwate and Yakumo visit.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3990 from Josephus Daniels Transmitting Report on Japanese Training Ships

subfiles.about: Detailed report on the September 1936 visit of Japanese training ships Iwate and Yakumo under Vice Admiral Zengo Yoshida to Manzanillo and Mexico City.
subfiles.summary: Military Attaché reports the 1936 visit of the Iwate and Yakumo, the drowning of three sailors and cadets clearing railway washouts.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Military Attaché on Visit of Japanese Training Ships Iwate and Yakumo

subfiles.about: Routing note drawing attention to consular reporting that the Japanese tanker Itsukushima Maru was under charter to British interests.
subfiles.summary: NOB tells Duggan the tanker Itsukushima Maru was under British charter.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from NOB to Laurence Duggan on British Charter of Japanese Tanker

subfiles.about: Transmits strictly confidential intelligence from Tampico regarding the expected arrival of the Japanese vessel Itsukushima Maru to take on petroleum.
subfiles.summary: Daniels forwards Tampico's report on the expected arrival of the tanker Itsukushima Maru, March 1938.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 120 from Josephus Daniels on Expected Arrival of Tanker Itsukushima Maru

subfiles.about: Reports on the chartering of the Itsukushima Maru and Danish tankers by Centralamer Ltd. to load Petromex oil at Tampico and Tuxpan.
subfiles.summary: Armstrong reports the Itsukushima Maru chartered by Centralamer to load Mexican oil, and Petromex's weak finances.
subfiles.title: Letter from L. S. Armstrong to Josephus Daniels on Oil Shipments and Centralamer Ltd.
